sources_considered.why: Reports self-critique experiments and improvements using the model's own critiques before the post.
Read to verify the June 12 submission and June 14 revision dates; the full paper is cited.
Later self-correction research concerns a different model period and cannot settle this historical claim.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; William Saunders and colleagues, OpenAI
evidence_items.locator: Abstract; methods and results in Sections 2, 4.2 and 4.3
evidence_items.explanation: The experiments evaluate models critiquing their own outputs against supplied passages or task constraints, and using critiques to improve answers. This contradicts the functional claim of complete inability, while leaving the nature of internal cognitive representations unsettled.

unresolved_gaps: The experiments do not identify an explicit cognitive world model inside the network.
Summarization judgments lacked fully objective ground truth, and the authors acknowledge evaluation errors.
The study does not establish reliable self-correction across unrestricted tasks.
